name: Iron deficiency pattern
association_text: Low hemoglobin with smaller-than-usual red cells and low iron stores is the pattern most often associated with iron deficiency anemia. MedlinePlus lists iron deficiency anemia as a cause of a low MCV and of low ferritin, and lists a lack of iron among the causes of low hemoglobin.

name: Low iron stores
association_text: Low ferritin with low serum iron suggests the body's iron stores are low. MedlinePlus lists iron deficiency anemia among the causes of both a low ferritin result and a low serum iron result.

name: Possible vitamin B12 deficiency pattern
association_text: Larger-than-usual red cells together with a low vitamin B12 result is the pattern MedlinePlus associates with pernicious anemia, which it describes as caused by a lack of vitamin B12 or by a condition that affects how the body uses it.

name: Possible folate deficiency pattern
association_text: Larger-than-usual red cells with a low folate result matches what MedlinePlus describes as anemia caused by a lack of folic acid.

name: Low hemoglobin
association_text: A low hemoglobin result is often the first sign of anemia. MedlinePlus lists several possible causes, including iron or vitamin B12 deficiency, blood loss, thalassemia, liver disease and other conditions. The test alone cannot show which of these applies.

name: HbA1c in the prediabetes range
association_text: MedlinePlus gives an HbA1c of 5.7% to 6.4% as the prediabetes range. It notes that providers often use more than one test to diagnose diabetes, such as a fasting glucose or an oral glucose tolerance test.

name: HbA1c in the diabetes range
association_text: MedlinePlus gives an HbA1c of 6.5% or higher as the diabetes range, and notes that providers often confirm with another test. It also notes that anemia and other blood disorders, kidney failure and liver disease can make this test inaccurate.

name: Fasting glucose and HbA1c both raised
association_text: A raised fasting glucose alongside a raised HbA1c means both a single measurement and the two-to-three-month average are above the usual range. MedlinePlus names prediabetes and diabetes as the most common causes of a high glucose result.

name: Raised liver enzymes
association_text: ALT and AST raised together is a pattern MedlinePlus associates with liver damage or disease, and it lists hepatitis, cirrhosis, certain medicines and alcohol among possible causes. AST is also found in heart and muscle tissue, so a raised AST is not specific to the liver.

name: Raised kidney markers
association_text: Creatinine and BUN raised together may mean the kidneys are not filtering as well as usual. MedlinePlus also lists non-kidney causes for each, including dehydration, a high-protein diet and muscle injury, so this pattern alone does not establish kidney disease.

name: Unfavourable lipid pattern
association_text: A raised LDL with a low HDL is the combination MedlinePlus describes as least favourable: it calls LDL the main source of artery blockages and says HDL helps remove LDL from the blood. It lists diet high in saturated fat, excess weight, smoking, inactivity, stress and alcohol among the things that raise cholesterol.

name: Raised triglycerides
association_text: MedlinePlus gives adult triglyceride bands of under 150 mg/dL healthy, 150-199 borderline high, 200-499 high and 500 or more very high, and notes that high levels usually cause no symptoms. Among the causes it lists are a diet high in fat, sugar and refined carbohydrate, inactivity, poorly controlled diabetes, kidney, liver or thyroid disease and some medicines.

name: TSH above the usual range
association_text: A higher-than-usual TSH may mean the body has too little thyroid hormone (hypothyroidism); MedlinePlus names Hashimoto's disease as the most common cause. It also notes TSH can be high when the thyroid is healthy, for example during serious illness, over age 80 or in pregnancy.

name: TSH below the usual range
association_text: A lower-than-usual TSH may mean too much thyroid hormone (hyperthyroidism); MedlinePlus names Graves' disease as the most common cause, and notes a low level can also occur briefly in serious illness unrelated to the thyroid and often in the first three months of pregnancy.

name: Vitamin D below the usual range
association_text: MedlinePlus says a low vitamin D result may mean too little vitamin D from diet or sunlight, trouble absorbing it from food, trouble converting it into a usable form, or a medicine that affects the level. It notes vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium for bones and teeth.

name: Albumin below the usual range
association_text: MedlinePlus lists liver disease, kidney disease, malnutrition with too little dietary protein, infection, digestive diseases that affect protein absorption, extensive burns and thyroid disease among possible reasons for a low albumin.

name: eGFR below 90
association_text: MedlinePlus gives an eGFR of 60 to 90 as possibly early-stage kidney disease, 15 to 60 as possibly kidney disease and below 15 as possibly kidney failure. It also notes an abnormal result is possible without kidney damage, and that results vary with age, body size, diet, muscle mass and medicines.

name: Platelet count below the usual range
association_text: MedlinePlus lists blood cancers, viral infections such as mononucleosis, hepatitis or measles, autoimmune disease, bone marrow infection or damage, cirrhosis, vitamin B12 deficiency and gestational thrombocytopenia among possible reasons for a low platelet count.

name: White cell count above the usual range
association_text: MedlinePlus lists infection, inflammatory diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis, allergies, leukemia or Hodgkin disease, tissue damage from a burn or surgery, and also smoking, stress, a reaction to a medicine or pregnancy among reasons a white cell count may be high.

name: White cell count below the usual range
association_text: MedlinePlus lists bone marrow damage from infection, disease or treatments such as chemotherapy, cancers affecting the bone marrow, autoimmune disorders, HIV, diseases of the liver or spleen and certain medicines among reasons a white cell count may be low.
